newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Soil disease killed 19 in Singapore in 1996 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Soil disease killed 19 in Singapore in 1996 - paper.

text.p: The mysterious soil disease melioidosis killed 19 people and infected 70 in Singapore last year, the Straits Times newspaper said on Monday.
It said there had been little advance in efforts to find a cure or improve diagnosis or treatment of the disease, found mainly in Southeast Asia.
"Doctors do not know why people die from it despite intensive treatment, or how it can remain dormant for years and then become active suddenly," the paper said.

The disease, believed to be a major killer in Thailand, is caused by bacteria found in wet soil and on the surface of muddy water. Symptoms of the disease include blood poisoning, chest infection and abscesses.
The paper quoted the Environment Ministry as saying that there had been 372 melioidosis cases in Singapore since 1989. The youngest victim was two and the oldest 91.
In 1995, 90 people were infected and 28 died, it said.
Government health and environment officials were unavailable to comment on Monday because of a public holiday.
